statement: The function returns a result r, and r equals the number of integers s such that there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries) and timeSeries[i] <= s < timeSeries[i] + duration. Equivalently, r is the cardinality of P = { s in Z | exists i, 0 <= i < len(timeSeries) and timeSeries[i] <= s < timeSeries[i] + duration }.
preconditions: 1 <= len(timeSeries) <= 10^4; 0 <= duration <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries), 0 <= timeSeries[i] <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries)-1, timeSeries[i] <= timeSeries[i+1].

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, overflow, or panic.
preconditions: 1 <= len(timeSeries) <= 10^4; 0 <= duration <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries), 0 <= timeSeries[i] <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries)-1, timeSeries[i] <= timeSeries[i+1].

statement: The function returns a result r and r >= duration.
preconditions: 1 <= len(timeSeries) <= 10^4; 0 <= duration <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries), 0 <= timeSeries[i] <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries)-1, timeSeries[i] <= timeSeries[i+1].

statement: The function returns a result r and r <= timeSeries[len(timeSeries)-1] - timeSeries[0] + duration.
preconditions: 1 <= len(timeSeries) <= 10^4; 0 <= duration <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries), 0 <= timeSeries[i] <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries)-1, timeSeries[i] <= timeSeries[i+1].

statement: Let D be the number of distinct values appearing in timeSeries, i.e. D = |{ timeSeries[i] | 0 <= i < len(timeSeries) }|. The function returns a result r and r >= D.
preconditions: 1 <= len(timeSeries) <= 10^4; 0 <= duration <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries), 0 <= timeSeries[i] <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries)-1, timeSeries[i] <= timeSeries[i+1]; duration >= 1.

statement: Let D be the number of distinct values appearing in timeSeries, i.e. D = |{ timeSeries[i] | 0 <= i < len(timeSeries) }|. The function returns a result r and r <= D * duration.
preconditions: 1 <= len(timeSeries) <= 10^4; 0 <= duration <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries), 0 <= timeSeries[i] <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries)-1, timeSeries[i] <= timeSeries[i+1].

statement: The function returns a result r and r = timeSeries[len(timeSeries)-1] - timeSeries[0] + duration.
preconditions: 1 <= len(timeSeries) <= 10^4; 0 <= duration <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries), 0 <= timeSeries[i] <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries)-1, timeSeries[i] <= timeSeries[i+1]; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries)-1, timeSeries[i+1] - timeSeries[i] <= duration.

statement: For every index i with 0 < i < len(timeSeries) and timeSeries[i] = timeSeries[i-1], let timeSeries' be the slice of length len(timeSeries)-1 obtained by deleting index i, so timeSeries'[j] = timeSeries[j] for j < i and timeSeries'[j] = timeSeries[j+1] for j >= i. Then find_poisoned_duration(timeSeries', duration) returns r' and find_poisoned_duration(timeSeries, duration) returns r, and r' = r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(timeSeries) <= 10^4; 0 <= duration <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries), 0 <= timeSeries[i] <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries)-1, timeSeries[i] <= timeSeries[i+1]; there exists an index i with 0 < i < len(timeSeries) and timeSeries[i] = timeSeries[i-1].

statement: Let timeSeries' be the slice with timeSeries'[j] = timeSeries[j] + c for every j with 0 <= j < len(timeSeries). Then find_poisoned_duration(timeSeries', duration) returns r' and find_poisoned_duration(timeSeries, duration) returns r, and r' = r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(timeSeries) <= 10^4; 0 <= duration <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries), 0 <= timeSeries[i] <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries)-1, timeSeries[i] <= timeSeries[i+1]; for every integer c such that 0 <= timeSeries[j] + c <= 10^7 for all j with 0 <= j < len(timeSeries).

statement: For every d1 and d2 with 0 <= d1 <= d2 <= 10^7, find_poisoned_duration(timeSeries, d1) returns r1 and find_poisoned_duration(timeSeries, d2) returns r2, and r1 <= r2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(timeSeries) <= 10^4; 0 <= duration <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries), 0 <= timeSeries[i] <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries)-1, timeSeries[i] <= timeSeries[i+1].

statement: Let P = { s in Z | exists i, 0 <= i < len(timeSeries) and timeSeries[i] <= s < timeSeries[i] + duration }. The function returns a result r and P has minimum timeSeries[0] and maximum timeSeries[len(timeSeries)-1] + duration - 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(timeSeries) <= 10^4; 0 <= duration <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries), 0 <= timeSeries[i] <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries)-1, timeSeries[i] <= timeSeries[i+1]; duration >= 1.

statement: Let n = len(timeSeries). The function returns a result r and r = duration + sum_{i=0}^{n-2} min(duration, timeSeries[i+1] - timeSeries[i]). This sum is empty when n = 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(timeSeries) <= 10^4; 0 <= duration <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries), 0 <= timeSeries[i] <= 10^7; for every i with 0 <= i < len(timeSeries)-1, timeSeries[i] <= timeSeries[i+1].
